 ET Online November 4 rain forecast
 The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued heavy rainfall warning s for several parts of the country on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Coastal Andhra Pradesh is likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places, while Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu-Puducherry and South Interior Karnataka may also experience heavy showers. The warnings come after Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast and weakened. The weather department has also cautioned about thunderstorms, lightning and strong surface winds in some areas.
 The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the westcentral Bay of Bengal and along the Andhra Pradesh coast during the warning period. Rough sea conditions are expected to persist even as wind speeds gradually ease.
 IMD rainfall forecast for November 4: State-wise weather updates
 Andhra Pradesh: Heavy to very heavy rainfall likely
Coastal Andhra Pradesh is likely to receive light to moderate rainfall at most places, with heavy to very heavy showers at isolated locations on Wednesday.

The warning covers districts including Krishna, Bapatla, Prakasam, SPSR Nellore, Guntur, Eluru, NTR, Palnadu and West Godavari. Thunderstorms, lightning and strong surface winds are also likely in parts of the state.
 Live Events
 The IMD has warned of a moderate flash flood risk in some watersheds and neighbouring areas of Bapatla, Eluru, Guntur, Krishna, NTR and Palnadu districts. Residents in low-lying areas have been advised to follow local administration instructions.
 Telangana: Heavy rain likely in parts of the state
Isolated heavy rainfall is likely over Telangana on November 4. This follows heavy to very heavy rainfall, including extremely heavy showers at isolated places in eastern Telangana on Tuesday.
 The IMD has also flagged a moderate flash flood risk in some watersheds, including areas in Nalgonda, Nagarkurnool and Suryapet. Residents should remain alert, particularly in locations that have already received significant rainfall.
 Chhattisgarh: Heavy showers likely to continue
Chhattisgarh is likely to receive light to moderate rainfall at many places, with heavy showers at isolated locations on Wednesday. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds may also occur in some areas.
Residents have been advised to monitor local weather updates and take precautions in areas prone to waterlogging.
 Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka: Heavy rainfall warning
The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places in Kerala and Mahe, Tamil Nadu-Puducherry-Karaikal and South Interior Karnataka on November 4.
Thunderstorms and lightning may accompany rainfall in some areas. People in affected districts should follow local weather advisories, especially while travelling.
 Odisha: No similar heavy rain warning specified for November 4
Parts of South Odisha were under a heavy rainfall warning on November 3. However, the latest forecast does not specify a similar heavy rainfall warning for the state on November 4. Coastal areas should continue to monitor local advisories, particularly those related to wind and sea conditions.
 IMD wind warning today: Strong winds over Bay of Bengal
The IMD has forecast a gradual reduction in wind speeds over parts of the Bay of Bengal as Cyclonic Storm Murasu weakens. However, strong winds and squally conditions may continue over parts of the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Residents in coastal areas have been advised to follow official warnings and avoid unnecessary movement during periods of strong winds and thunderstorms.
 Sea conditions today: Fishermen advised not to venture out
The IMD has warned of rough to very rough sea conditions over parts of the westcentral Bay of Bengal and along the Andhra Pradesh coast. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the westcentral Bay of Bengal and along and off the Andhra Pradesh coast during the warning period, which extends into Wednesday.
The advisory also covers affected coastal waters around the region. Fishermen should follow the latest IMD bulletins and instructions from local authorities before resuming fishing activities.
Residents in coastal districts and areas prone to waterlogging or flooding are advised to monitor weather updates and follow safety instructions issued by the IMD and local administrations.
